findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/MeasurableIntegral.lean:56 `theorem StronglyMeasurable.integral_kernel ⦃f : β → E⦄ (hf : StronglyMeasurable f) : StronglyMeasurable fun x ↦ ∫ y, f y ∂κ x`, preceded by `omit [IsSFiniteKernel κ]`; :34 `measurableSet_integrable`. `Kernel` is `structure Kernel (α β) where toFun; measurable'` (Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/Defs.lean:55) and `ProbabilityMeasure` carries the subtype σ-algebra (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/ProbabilityMeasure.lean:247), which is why the PR's own proof uses `measurable_subtype_coe`.
findings.fix: Drop `{C} (hbdd)` and the ∫⁻-splitting proof; take the coercion kernel: `theorem measurable_probabilityMeasure_integral {f : α → ℝ} (hf : StronglyMeasurable f) : Measurable fun P : ProbabilityMeasure α => ∫ y, f y ∂(P : Measure α) := (hf.integral_kernel (κ := ⟨fun P : ProbabilityMeasure α => (P : Measure α), measurable_subtype_coe⟩)).measurable`, and correct the module docstring, which currently states the Bochner case is unavailable. Callers in ConditionallyIID/StrongLaw.lean:113 then pass `hf.stronglyMeasurable` only.
findings.issue: `measurable_probabilityMeasure_integral` is a strictly weaker special case of Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.integral_kernel`, which gives `StronglyMeasurable fun x => ∫ y, f y ∂κ x` for any kernel `κ` and strongly measurable `f` — no boundedness, and no s-finiteness (the lemma carries `omit [IsSFiniteKernel κ]`). The junk-value handling the module docstring claims is missing is done there by `ProbabilityTheory.measurableSet_integrable`.

findings.issue: `hmapf` (73–76), `hident` (79–81) and `hlimit` (87–88) re-derive Mathlib's `HasLaw` API by hand: the map-composition computation, the identical distribution of `f ∘ eval i`, and the identification of the limit.

summary: The new almost-sure results are genuinely new (TauCeti has only the mean-square form), but the supporting material re-derives located API: the ProbabilityMeasure integral-measurability lemma is a bounded special case of Mathlib's `StronglyMeasurable.integral_kernel`, and `strong_law_ae_infinitePi`'s preamble re-proves `HasLaw`/`IdentDistrib` facts that Mathlib and a private HewittSavage lemma already provide.
